business_problem: Public defenders had to review audiovisual evidence manually, often after receiving it in inconsistent formats and dealing with incompatible files and video players. Reviewing hours of footage in real time left under-resourced attorneys with less time for other case work.
solution_summary: JusticeText accepts audiovisual discovery through attorney uploads or file synchronization; the source says materials may arrive via USB drives, cloud links, or email, and identifies body-worn-camera footage, interrogation videos, jail calls, and other evidence. The platform analyzes those materials with AI to produce full transcripts and summaries and flag legal events such as Miranda warnings and sobriety tests. Attorneys can search the resulting documents by keyword, isolate and generate clips, add notes, and collaborate in a centralized platform. Miranda AI adds a legal-specific assistant for building timelines, surfacing inconsistencies, and extracting facts aligned with a defense strategy. The account does not identify underlying speech or video models, storage technology, hosting, APIs, or integrations, so those implementation details cannot be specified.
